rationale:
Evidence: iteration 3 (y = 0.06 m, last_direction, score 49.94) is the best raced design. Every trial in every iteration ends off track with one line-loss event and max_error censored near 0.061 m. Iterations 0 and 2 gave identical results across large kp, ki and kd changes, so gains do not reach the first loss. Iteration 5 (search_left at the iteration 4 geometry) left the s-bend (0.1451) and slalom (0.1041) unchanged to four decimals and moved only the oval (46.33 to 43.25). The recovery direction therefore has no measured effect on two of three tracks.

Critique handling. Accepted: the forced signal change under search_right can cause a derivative kick at the first loss, so the result may partly reflect the kick and not the direction. The contract does not show whether line-loss signals pass through the derivative term, and I cannot remove that confound without a second variable. I keep the single-variable test and will read steering_oscillation and control_effort alongside the score to see whether a kick is present. Accepted: the first-loss step is not returned by the requested measurements, so I remove that decision rule. Accepted: the expected result must be falsifiable. Rejected: a move to start-alignment or speed tests in this round, since that would add variables and make the result unattributable.

Change: line_loss from last_direction to search_right. Everything else matches iteration 3: five sensors at x = -0.03 to +0.03 m, y = 0.06 m, 0.016 m footprint, weights [-1.5, -0.75, 0, 0.75, 1.5], kp 2.0, ki 0.1, kd 0.1, base_speed 1.4, wheel_track 0.12 m, mass 0.8 kg.

Falsifiable expectation: s-bend and slalom progress will be within 0.0005 of iteration 3 (0.1475 and 0.1041), consistent with iteration 5, so the recovery rule does not matter on those tracks. If the oval score moves by more than the seed spread (about 45.3 to 47.3), the direction matters there. Any progress rise above 0.02 on any track would contradict iteration 5 and would be a real finding. Decision: keep search_right only if the score beats 49.94 with no larger steering_oscillation; otherwise return to last_direction. Speed stays at 1.4 this round. If this result is null, base_speed becomes the next single-variable test, since completion is still unmeasured and there are few iterations left.
